issue.title: fetchkit gives up immediately when the server answers 503
issue.body:
Our CDN returned a 503 for a few seconds during a deploy and fetchkit failed right away:

    $ fetchkit https://cdn.example.com/build/app.tar.gz -o app.tar.gz
    error: HTTP 503 for https://cdn.example.com/build/app.tar.gz

It returned instantly, there was no waiting at all. Running it again 10 seconds later worked. Our previous download tool would have ridden out the blip.

I'm using the defaults, no flags. fetchkit 0.3.1, Python 3.12 on Linux.

files.README.md:
# fetchkit

A small HTTP download helper with a friendly CLI.

    fetchkit URL [-o FILE]

commits.message: Add retry helper with exponential backoff

files.README.md:
# fetchkit

A small HTTP download helper with a friendly CLI.

    fetchkit URL [-o FILE]

## Reliability

fetchkit retries a request up to `retries` times (default 3) when it hits a connection error, a timeout or an HTTP 5xx response, waiting `backoff * 2**attempt` seconds between attempts. 4xx responses are never retried.

files.fetchkit/cli.py:
import argparse
import sys

from .client import Client
from .errors import FetchError


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='fetchkit')
    parser.add_argument('url')
    parser.add_argument('-o', '--output', help='write the body to this file')
    parser.add_argument('--retries', type=int, default=3)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    client = Client(retries=args.retries)
    try:
        resp = client.get(args.url)
    except FetchError as exc:
        print(f'error: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if args.output:
        with open(args.output, 'wb') as fh:
            fh.write(resp.body)
    else:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(resp.body)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

expected.cause: Only ConnectionError and TimeoutError are retried, while an HTTP 5xx is returned as a normal Response and turned into HTTPStatusError after the retry wrapper has finished, so 5xx responses are never retried although the README promises it.

notes: Docs/code disagreement: README promises retries on HTTP 5xx. The issue never mentions the README. Check client.py: line 24-25 swallow HTTPError into a Response, 27-31 raise after with_retries.
